headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from ChatGPT Desktop ingesting content while the repo is a content-writing source with no isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent B can read clipboard, files, screenshots, and app content by default, so content from Agent A can be ingested as trusted text if the operator bridges them. Agent A is a content-writing repository with no isolation or provenance controls, so prompt-like material could be passed through and misread as instructions. The pairwise pathway exists, but only via shared content channels.
conditions: IF the operator copies Agent A output into Agent B clipboard or files
IF Agent B is asked to summarize or act on content from Agent A without provenance labels
mitigations: Use explicit delimiters and provenance labels for any Agent A content pasted into Agent B
Disable clipboard-based handoff during review sessions
Require a human to strip instructions from Agent A outputs before reuse
Keep Agent A outputs in read-only notes rather than executable prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware parsing between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent B can read uploaded files, screenshots, and files from supported macOS apps, so any sensitive material handled by Agent A can be exposed if the operator shares the same workspace or clipboard. Agent A itself has no declared data classes or protections, so the main leakage risk is B ingesting and transmitting that content to its vendor backend. This is a default-capable workspace leak, not a provable none.
conditions: IF Agent A outputs are stored in files or app windows readable by Agent B
IF those files contain secrets, personal data, or confidential work products
mitigations: Keep Agent A outputs in a separate local workspace
Avoid pasting sensitive content into Agent B
Use redacted excerpts instead of full documents
Turn off screenshot-based handoff when not needed
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A exposes no write or network capabilities in the profile, while Agent B cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is read-side interaction through files and app content, so the pairwise conflict surface is limited.
conditions: IF Agent A is manually used to generate content that Agent B then edits elsewhere
IF a third-party orchestrator grants both agents write access outside these profiles
mitigations: Keep Agent A read-only in the workflow
Do not let Agent B edit shared git or filesystem state
Use one-way export from Agent A to Agent B
Review any shared mutable resource before handoff
requires-engineering: add locking for shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B can treat imported files, screenshots, or app context as input, so Agent A-generated content may flow into B without verification. Agent A is a prompt-engineering content source, which increases the chance that B will render or act on persuasive but unverified instructions. The pairwise cascade is plausible in default workflows, though not proven automatic.
conditions: IF Agent A output is pasted into Agent B as task context
IF Agent B is instructed to act on Agent A content without a verification step
mitigations: Require a verification step before Agent B acts on Agent A output
Ask Agent B to cite source lines before using claims
Use a human approval gate for any action derived from Agent A
Separate drafting from execution roles
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking or provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Agent B is a closed-source desktop product with vendor-only egress and documented handling of uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and app content; Agent A is an open-source content-writing repo with no declared regulated-data handling. No specific residency or certification mismatch is evidenced here, so the compliance risk is limited to documented-policy gaps rather than a clear breach. Agent A is cited only to show the pair context.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Agent B inputs
IF the operator expects Agent A content to inherit a stricter retention or residency policy than Agent B provides
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to Agent B
Check retention settings before use
Use de-identified examples for drafting
Document which agent handles which data class
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across the workflow
